Content generator project

In the Studio you type one idea, say whether it is a physical product, an app, a service or a space, pick a visual direction, and press Forge Prototype. You can also start from a scenario such as Health, Mobility, Fintech or Education, or queue several ideas in a batch.

Prompt engineering case study

Goal: turn a rough one-line idea into four visuals that all describe the same product.

Approach: instead of sending the raw idea to every image step, an optimizer first rewrites it into a structured brief. The sketch, render, scenario and ad all start from that one brief, so they stay consistent.

Open and view application View code
Sentiment analysis project

Three steps, then scroll. Upload any CSV, TSV or TXT of written comments such as reviews, surveys or tickets, choose the text column, and every comment is scored positive, neutral or negative. Optional columns for groups, dates and star ratings unlock more charts, and themes are found automatically or taken from a preset.

Data insights report

Findings from the built-in fictional patient-feedback sample (12 comments), written by the app itself in plain English.

Overall moodAn average score of +0.15, with 58% positive and 42% negative comments.
Strongest themeService Quality, with an average of +0.27 and 60% positive.
Polarised themeStaff is 40% positive and 40% negative, so the average hides strong opposing views.
Over timeSentiment improved from -0.01 on 2 March to +0.22 on 6 April.
Negative wordsThe most common words in negative comments were told, hour, staff, rude and nobody.
Technical explanation
  1. Upload: the user adds a CSV, TSV or TXT file, or ticks a built-in fictional sample.
  2. Choose columns: the user picks the text column, and optionally a group, date and rating column.
  3. Score: VADER, a rule-based sentiment tool built for short written text, scores each sentence, and the score becomes positive, neutral or negative.
  4. Find themes: themes are discovered automatically or taken from a preset, and a comment can speak to several themes.
  5. Visualise: charts are drawn on black panels in a custom dotted-art style, with plain-English insights beside them.
  6. Export: results can be downloaded as a scored CSV or a text file of insights.
  7. Deploy: the code lives on GitHub and runs on Streamlit Community Cloud.

Scoring is designed for English text. Project files: app.py, art.py, requirements.txt and config.toml.
